findings.claim: SAF-D2-001 carry-forward (fr2 false-close): _build_snapshot reads and parses docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub without exception handling; a RuntimeError from _parse_signing_keys (no current marker, multiple current markers, git-show failure for missing file) still propagates upward, preventing self._snapshot from updating and making all 11 resource URIs unavailable until a corrective commit. Each failed request incurs two git subprocess calls (_head_commit + git show signing-keys), constituting a subprocess-fan-out DoS under 021H concurrent load.
findings.evidence: resources.py:541-546: signing_keys_text = _read_committed_text(self._repo_root, ref, 'docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub') and signing_keys_body = _parse_signing_keys(signing_keys_text) — no enclosing try/except. _parse_signing_keys raises RuntimeError at line 255 (len(current_entries)>1) and lines 258-262 (not current_entries and keys). _build_snapshot is called inside the _snapshot_lock at snapshot() line 452; if it raises, line 453 (self._snapshot = snapshot) never executes. Subsequent reads re-enter _build_snapshot, each spawning git subprocesses before raising again. Grep for 'try:' in _build_snapshot body confirms no exception handler present.
findings.impact: A careless or hostile committer corrupting docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub (format error, missing current marker, duplicate current marker) causes total MCP service outage. Operators see errors on scp://rules/registry or scp://findings/open with no causal link to the signing-keys file. Under 021H concurrent HTTP load each failed request amplifies subprocess CPU load proportionally to request rate until a corrective commit lands. Failure is non-recoverable without a new commit.
findings.mitigation: In _build_snapshot, wrap lines 541-546 in a try/except (RuntimeError, Exception) as signing_key_err block. On failure: set current_key_id=None and signing_keys_resource = _resource_envelope({'error': str(signing_key_err), 'keys': [], 'current_key': None, 'current_key_sha256': None, 'prior_keys': [], 'trust_model': {}}, key_id=None). Allow _build_snapshot to proceed with key_id=None for all other resources. Isolates signing-keys errors to scp://security/signing-keys only, leaving the remaining 10 resource URIs operational.

findings.claim: SAF-D2-002 carry-forward: trust_model.adopter_requirement (resources.py:277-279) still contains 'or a pinned sha256', permitting adopters to implement resource-only verification where both public_key and current_key_sha256 are sourced from the same substitutable MCP response. A transport MITM who replaces current_key.public_key with their own Ed25519 key and updates current_key_sha256 to its SHA-256 defeats the adopter's resource-only cross-check. The consult-receipt verification gate — the core integrity primitive of WP-SCP-021 — remains bypassable for HTTP-mode adopters.
findings.evidence: resources.py:277-279: adopter_requirement = ('Cross-check the MCP-delivered current key against the committed keyring or a pinned sha256 before trusting consult-receipt verification.'). current_key_sha256 (line 269) is derived from current_key.public_key_sha256 in the same response payload. A MITM need only update both fields atomically; the 'or a pinned sha256' clause permits adopters to check public_key against current_key_sha256 from the same response, which the MITM controls. 021F adopter guide not written; no enforced specification prohibits resource-only verification.
findings.impact: Adopters who implement the 'or a pinned sha256' path using the in-response digest are not protected against MITM substitution. The Ed25519 consult-receipt verification gate becomes a dead letter for such adopters until 021H TLS ships. Since 021F has not been written, there is no mechanised enforcement of the committed-file cross-check requirement.
findings.mitigation: Option A (immediate): Replace 'or a pinned sha256' with: 'You MUST cross-check the MCP-delivered current key against docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub in the committed repository. The current_key_sha256 field is a convenience digest, not an independent trust anchor — do not use it as a standalone pin.' Option B (021F): Adopter guide must explicitly prohibit using in-response current_key_sha256 as a pin without external backing.

findings.claim: CG-R2-002 carry-forward (fr2 false-close): server.py instructions field (lines 45-47) still reads 'Standards Control Plane MCP scaffold. Tools and resources are introduced in later implementation slices.' Both tools (021C) and resources (021D) are fully registered via __post_init__ (lines 57-61). Every connecting MCP client receives an instructions string asserting the server has no current capabilities.
findings.evidence: server.py:45-47: instructions: str = ('Standards Control Plane MCP scaffold. Tools and resources are introduced ' 'in later implementation slices.'). __post_init__ lines 57-61: register_tools(self._server) and register_resources(self._server) called unconditionally. No test asserts instructions field content. fr2 commit names 'server.py instructions' as a closed item; direct read of server.py confirms the text is unchanged.
findings.impact: MCP clients (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) receive an instructions string declaring the server is a placeholder with future capabilities, contradicting its registered surface. An adopter using the instructions field for capability discovery would bypass the server entirely. The mismatch undermines governance completeness for any external reviewer auditing 021D.
findings.mitigation: Update server.py lines 45-47: instructions = ('Standards Control Plane MCP server. Resources: scp://rules/registry, scp://rules/domain-map, scp://decisions, scp://findings/open, scp://waivers, scp://status, scp://security/signing-keys, plus per-ID templates (scp://rule/{rule_id}, scp://waiver/{waiver_id}, scp://finding/{finding_id}, scp://decision/{decision_id}). Tools: audit_changed, consult_rules, check_finding, check_waiver, propose, list_open_decisions, resolve_domain.'). Add a test asserting 'scp://rules/registry' appears in ScpMcpServer().instructions.

findings.claim: CG-R2-001 carry-forward (fr2 false-close): WP-SCP-021 §13 unknowns table rows for U-21-b, U-21-e, U-21-h carry no Resolution column. Three load-bearing design decisions — resource-update notification client support matrix, direct registry exposure without façade, domain-map derivation from registry — remain undocumented. fr2 commit claims 'U-21 closures'; plan file is unchanged.
findings.evidence: docs/plans/WP-SCP-021-scp-as-mcp-server.md lines 246, 249, 252: rows for U-21-b ('MCP client support for progress + resource-update notifications (Claude Code, Desktop, Cursor, Codex) | 021D'), U-21-e ('scp://rules/registry internal shape stability — expose direct or via façade? | 021D'), U-21-h ('scp://rules/domain-map source-of-truth — derived from registry or authored separately? | 021D') have original text only. Table header at line 244 shows three columns (blank, description, target-slice); no Resolution column present anywhere in §13.
findings.impact: Future operators cannot distinguish deliberate design choice from accidental outcome. U-21-b is operationally critical for 021F adopter hooks: without a recorded client-support matrix, adopters cannot safely implement re-polling fallback for non-subscribing clients. The 021F reviewer has no governance checkpoint to verify U-21-b was consciously resolved.
findings.mitigation: Append a Resolution column to the WP-SCP-021 §13 unknowns table. U-21-b: 'FastMCP test harness verified subscribe=True; Claude Code / Desktop / Codex client matrix deferred to 021F adopter guide; re-polling fallback required for non-subscribing clients.' U-21-e: 'Direct exposure accepted; façade deferred pending registry schema-version stability.' U-21-h: 'Derived from registry applies_to in _build_domain_map; separate authoring rejected.' No code change required.

findings.claim: Empty or all-comment signing-keys file silently degrades to key_id=None in all resource envelopes with no error raised and no operational signal. The guard 'if not current_entries and keys' (resources.py:256) requires the file to contain at least one parseable key line; a committed file with zero key lines (blank or all-comment) produces keys=[], bypasses both RuntimeError guards, returns current_key=None, and stamps key_id=None on all 11 resource envelopes. This is a distinct bypass path from SAF-D2-001 (which requires keys to be present but malformed): an empty keyring silently nullifies key integrity claims without triggering the SAF-D2-001 outage path, meaning it evades both the existing guard and the SAF-D2-001 try/except mitigation.
findings.evidence: resources.py:228-262: for-loop at line 228 populates keys[] only for lines passing 'len(parts) < 2 or parts[0] != "ssh-ed25519"' check. A file of only blank lines or '#'-prefixed comments exits the loop with keys=[]. Line 253: len(current_entries)>1 → False (current_entries=[]). Line 256: not current_entries and keys → True and False → False — no RuntimeError raised. Line 262: current_key = current_entries[0] if current_entries else None → None. resources.py:547-548: current_key_id = current_key.get('key_id') if isinstance(current_key, dict) else None → None. All _resource_envelope calls receive key_id=None. test_signing_keys.py has no test case for the empty-file path. The SAF-D2-001 try/except mitigation (when implemented) would not protect against this path as no exception is raised.
findings.impact: A developer who commits a blank mcp-signing-keys.pub during key rotation silently nullifies key_id across all MCP resource envelopes. Adopters relying on key_id for receipt verification silently receive resources with no key reference; the degradation is invisible in logs, MCP error responses, and resource payloads (key_id=null looks like a valid optional value). Unlike SAF-D2-001 which causes a visible outage, this path causes silent security degradation that persists until noticed through an audit. An adversary with repo write access can blank the file as a stealth operation.
findings.mitigation: Add a guard in _parse_signing_keys after the loop exits and before the current_entries checks: 'if not keys: raise RuntimeError("docs/security/mcp-signing-keys.pub contains no key entries; file may be blank or corrupted")'. This makes empty-file commits produce the same RuntimeError as malformed-file commits, ensuring the SAF-D2-001 mitigation (try/except wrapper) also catches this case. Add test: create repo with mcp-signing-keys.pub containing only a comment line; assert catalog.read_static('scp://security/signing-keys') surfaces an error (raises RuntimeError or returns envelope with 'error' key and key_id=None depending on which mitigation is applied first).

findings.claim: The 'multiple current signing keys' error path (resources.py:253-255) has no test coverage. test_signing_keys_require_exactly_one_current_marker (test_signing_keys.py:32-51) only exercises the 'no current marker' path. The len(current_entries)>1 branch is untested dead code from a CI perspective; the SB-MAJ-002 closure evidence acknowledged both error paths but the test only verifies one.
findings.evidence: test_signing_keys.py:38-42: fixture sets 'current=false' for the old key and omits any current=true marker for the new key; the test asserts RuntimeError match='no current signing key declared'. No test creates two keys both marked current=true and asserts RuntimeError match='multiple current signing keys declared'. resources.py:253-255: 'if len(current_entries) > 1: raise RuntimeError(f"multiple current signing keys declared: {key_ids}")' — this branch is unreachable in any current test scenario. The R2 SB-MAJ-002 closure evidence stated 'raises RuntimeError on zero current keys and on multiple current keys' but the test only exercised the zero-current path.
findings.impact: A future refactor that accidentally removes the multiple-current guard would not be caught by CI. A key rotation that inadvertently marks two keys as current would succeed silently rather than failing loudly, producing a resource surface that advertises two competing current keys.
findings.mitigation: Add test_signing_keys_rejects_multiple_current_markers to test_signing_keys.py: create_resource_repo with mcp-signing-keys.pub containing two keys both marked current=true; assert ScpCommittedResourceCatalog(repo_root=..., now_func=...).read_static('scp://security/signing-keys') raises RuntimeError with match='multiple current signing keys declared'.

findings.claim: SAF-D2-003 carry-forward: catalog.subscribe() accepts arbitrary URI strings with no validation against STATIC_RESOURCE_URIS or TEMPLATE_RESOURCE_URIS, enabling unbounded _subscribers dict growth and O(N_fabricated_uris) CPU work on every HEAD-change notification dispatch. No fix applied in fr2.
findings.evidence: resources.py:458-459: self._subscribers.setdefault(uri, set()).add(session) — no allow-list check. subscribe_resource handler lines 784-787: catalog.subscribe(str(uri), ...) with no URI validation. _schedule_resource_update_notifications lines 530-536: iterates all self._subscribers keys, calling _snapshot_payload_for_uri (prefix-scan loops over four snapshot dicts) for each entry including fabricated ones. No change to these lines in fr2.
findings.impact: On HTTP transport (021H), a client subscribing to K unique fabricated URIs before disconnecting permanently adds K entries to _subscribers. Each HEAD advance triggers K × len(sessions) _snapshot_payload_for_uri calls for garbage URIs. Compounds on high-frequency-commit repositories under CI merge load.
findings.mitigation: In subscribe_resource (lines 784-787), validate uri: reject URIs not in STATIC_RESOURCE_URIS and not prefixed by a TEMPLATE_RESOURCE_URIS stem. Return MCP error on invalid URI. Add per-session subscription cap in subscribe().

findings.claim: SAF-D2-004 carry-forward: loop.create_task(session.send_resource_updated(uri)) at resources.py:536 has no exception handler; failed sessions (disconnected clients that did not cleanly MCP-unsubscribe) are never removed from _subscribers and receive new create_task calls on every subsequent HEAD advance. No fix applied in fr2.
findings.evidence: resources.py:536: loop.create_task(session.send_resource_updated(uri)) — bare call, no try/except, no task.add_done_callback. unsubscribe_resource (lines 789-791) only invoked on clean MCP unsubscription; network-level disconnects do not trigger it. test_resource_notifications.py _FakeSession.send_resource_updated is a simple list append that never raises; failure path is unexercised. No change to these lines in fr2.
findings.impact: Sessions that fail on send_resource_updated accumulate in _subscribers indefinitely. Under asyncio default exception handler, failed Tasks are silently discarded. With multiple stale sessions, Task churn and subscriber set bloat compound with each HEAD advance.
findings.mitigation: Use a _safe_notify coroutine that catches exceptions and calls catalog.unsubscribe(uri, session). Dispatch via loop.create_task(_safe_notify(session, uri)). Add test that makes _FakeSession.send_resource_updated raise on second call and asserts session is removed from _subscribers.

structured_review.summary: R3 safety_bypass review of 021D after fr2. Fixpoint NOT reached. The fr2 commit claims to close 5 R2 MAJs; only COR2-D-001 (status test coverage) is confirmed closed. Three claimed closures are false: SAF-D2-001 (no try/except added in _build_snapshot), CG-R2-002 (server.py instructions text unchanged), CG-R2-001 (WP-SCP-021 §13 plan file unchanged). SAF-D2-002 (MITM bypass via substitutable payload) was not targeted by fr2 and remains open. A new MAJ (SAF-R3-001) is raised for the silent empty-signing-keys degradation path not covered by either the existing guards or the SAF-D2-001 try/except mitigation. 8 findings total: 5 MAJ, 3 MIN. Fixpoint requires 5 MAJ closures before §4.3 criteria can be assessed.
